messages:
lauren (Finance): Heads-up — Batch of reseller invoices from GCP marketplace (region: EU) show tiny FX rounding variances on prorated lines. Individually small (0.01-1.20 EUR) but aggregated across 1,900 lines = ~EUR 2,300 / USD ~2,480 exposure. Partners are asking for a single settlement adjustment instead of per-invoice micro-credits. @mohit @esteban please advise.
mohit (Partner Ops): We're seeing the rounding happen when prorates are generated during cross-currency conversions (EUR invoice, USD internal). The prorate engine applies per-line rounding which causes net drift. I can share mapping and sample invoices. @billing-bot can you pull sample invoice ids for partners affected (top 5 by amount) for Apr 20-30?
billing-bot: Query complete. Sample invoices: GCP-INV-43210, GCP-INV-43211, GCP-INV-43215, GCP-INV-43302, GCP-INV-43308. Affected prorate lines: 1,897. Aggregate variance: EUR 2,305.12 (USD 2,485.60). Created internal ticket FIN-3950. CSV uploaded: https://redwood.internal/drive/gcp-eu-fx-prorate-variance.csv
esteban (Sales): Partners requested a single net settlement adjustment credited to their partner account rather than chasing micro-credits for each end-customer. They prefer ledger credit (one line) for easier reconciliation.
zara (Accounting): From accounting perspective, we prefer to post a single contra entry per partner to clear the exposure. Need guidance on GL mapping and whether to treat as "rounding adjustments" (GL 4230) or "partner rebates" (GL 4210). Also need to ensure audit trail with per-invoice detail attached.
kevin (RevOps): Operationally we can: 1) generate a consolidated settlement adjustment per partner referencing FIN-3950 and attach the CSV with per-invoice breakdown, 2) post provisional journals reversing the tiny variances to GL 4230, then reclass to 4210 if partner insists. Which GL do we want as default?
lauren (Finance): Tax/Revenue intent: these are rounding diffs not commercial rebates, treat as rounding adjustments. Proposal: GL 4230 (Marketplace rounding adjustments). But if partner has contractual claim to rebates, we can reclass later with evidence. Attach per-invoice CSV.
mohit (Partner Ops): I'll notify affected partners with proposed single settlement adjustment and attach FIN-3950 detail. Will ask them to confirm acceptance of consolidated credit or if they want per-invoice credits for specific end-customers.
zara (Accounting): Please include a note that for external audit we will keep the invoice-level CSV and the single credit memo will reference each invoice id. Also request partner acceptance email for our records.
kevin (RevOps): Draft credit memo template for partner settlement (one per partner):

"Credit memo to Partner (partner id: <PARTNER_ID>)
Amount: EUR <AGG_AMOUNT>
Reason: Aggregate FX/proration rounding adjustments across GCP marketplace prorate lines (see attached invoice-level breakdown).
Related invoices: list attached (CSV).
GL code: 4230 (Marketplace rounding adjustments)
Internal ticket: FIN-3950
Approvers: @lauren, @isabel (Finance Lead)"

isabel (Finance Lead): Approved to proceed with GL 4230 as default for rounding adjustments. Approve issuing consolidated settlement adjustments pending partner acceptance and attaching FIN-3950 evidence. :white_check_mark:
billing-bot: Consolidated settlement adjustment request created and queued for partner batch: SETTLE-BATCH-7622. Partners notified pending their acceptance. FIN-3950 linked. ETA processing 5-8 business days after acceptance.
lauren (Finance): I'll post provisional journal entries in the close workbook under "rounding exposures" and attach FIN-3950. Once partners accept, we'll convert to final credit memos and route to GCP settlement ops. Thanks team.
mohit (Partner Ops): Notifying partners now and will update the thread with any partner exceptions. :thumbsup:
